checks.title: Set up naming and PostScript names
checks.info:
Fill in the family name, style names and PostScript names in Font Info. Style names use title case (Bold Italic, not bold-italic), and PostScript names have no spaces or special characters.

Family plus style should stay under 63 characters. The Glyphs naming tutorial covers the rules for each type of name.

checks.title: Set up style linking
checks.info:
In Font Info > Exports, link the Bold, Italic and Bold Italic instances to their base style. Leave the other styles unlinked.

This is what makes the Bold and Italic buttons in Word and InDesign pick the right file. Testing it in real applications is a separate check under Final QA.

checks.title: Place the masters correctly in the designspace
checks.info:
Give each master its axis coordinates in Font Info > Masters, and keep every instance inside the range the masters cover.

Two masters at the same location cannot interpolate, and an axis needs masters at two different positions to work at all. Instances outside the range have to be extrapolated.

checks.title: Confirm the default master is the intended style
checks.info:
Check which master is the origin of the variable font: the Variable Font Origin parameter, or the first master if none is set.

Applications show the origin before any axis is moved, and fallback renderers use it. It should be the style the family leads with.

checks.title: Add the 'Use Typo Metrics' parameter
checks.info:
Add Use Typo Metrics in Font Info > Font, and fill in the typo metrics themselves.

With this set, applications take line spacing from the typo values instead of the win values. That gives the same spacing on macOS and Windows, and Google Fonts requires it.

checks.title: Complete the version number and font info
checks.info:
Set the version number and fill in designer, manufacturer, copyright and license in Font Info.

These fields are written into every exported file and show up in font managers and Get Info panels.

checks.title: Keep PostScript names within the length limits
checks.info:
Check that the PostScript name of every exporting instance is 63 characters or fewer.

Longer names break in older applications and some PDF workflows. Under 31 characters is safer if the family has to work in legacy software.

checks.title: Match weight and width names to their classes
checks.info:
Check that each instance's weight class and width class match its style name. Light should be 300, Condensed should be 3.

Applications sort styles and pick substitutes by these numbers rather than by the name. A wrong value puts styles in the wrong order in menus.

checks.title: Keep variable font names apart from the statics
checks.info:
When statics and a variable font come from the same file, give the variable font its own family name with the Variable Font Family Name parameter.

If both install under the same family name, the system keeps one and drops the other.

checks.title: Set the Vendor ID
checks.info:
Add the vendorID parameter in Font Info > Font. It has to be exactly four ASCII characters.

The vendor ID identifies the foundry in the OS/2 table and shows up in font managers. Microsoft keeps a register of them.

checks.title: Check the copyright years and ownership
checks.info:
Read the copyright string in Font Info and check the years, the owner, and that it agrees with the license text.

This is the notice that ships inside every file. Years and names carried over from an earlier project are common.

checks.title: Decide the PANOSE values deliberately
checks.info:
Either leave PANOSE unset, which means all zeros, or set values that describe the design.

All zeros means 'any' and is safe. Values left from another project affect how systems match and substitute the font.

checks.title: Give every glyph its expected Unicode value
checks.info:
Check that exporting glyphs which should have a codepoint have one.

Without a Unicode value a glyph can only be reached through a feature. It cannot be typed, copied or read by a screen reader. Glyphs assigns most codepoints from the glyph name.

checks.title: Remove duplicate Unicode values
checks.info:
Check that no two exporting glyphs have the same codepoint.

The cmap table maps each codepoint to one glyph, so only one of the two can be reached in the exported font.

checks.title: Follow the Google Fonts vertical metrics strategy
checks.info:
If the project targets Google Fonts, set the typo, hhea and win metrics in the relationship the Google Fonts guide describes, with a typo line gap of zero.

Following one strategy gives the same line spacing on macOS, Windows and in browsers. Fontspector checks the result on the compiled file.

checks.title: Keep uppercase diacritics below the clipping boundary
checks.info:
Check that the tallest glyphs, usually uppercase diacritics, stay inside the win metrics in every master.

Windows applications cut off anything above winAscent or below winDescent. Accented capitals are the first to go.

checks.title: Keep vertical metrics identical across masters
checks.info:
Check that every master has the same vertical metric values.

Metrics that differ between masters change the line spacing when the weight changes, and produce inconsistent interpolated instances.

checks.title: Keep line spacing consistent across the family
checks.info:
Compare the vertical metrics of every style: masters, instance overrides, and the other files of the family if they are open.

Setting text in Regular and switching it to Italic should not change the leading. Roman and italic kept in separate files are the usual source of a mismatch.

checks.title: Check that shapes match the alignment zones
checks.info:
Compare the overshoots of round shapes against the zones in Font Info > Masters. Overshoots belong inside the zone, flat shapes on the flat edge.

Zones that miss the shapes make hinting align the wrong outlines. This one stays manual: on real fonts, near misses are as often intended as not.

checks.title: Check that stem thickness is consistent
checks.info:
Compare vertical stems against each other, and horizontals against each other, across the alphabet and across masters.

Uneven stems show up as patchy colour in text. The Stem Thickness reporter measures stems under the cursor. Many designs vary stems on purpose, so the judgement stays with the designer.

checks.title: Check for almost-straight segments
checks.info:
Look for curve segments that are nearly straight and decide whether they should be straight.

These are usually drawing accidents, and they show as a slight wobble at large sizes. Red Arrow marks them in the edit view.

checks.title: Check for kinks in the outlines
checks.info:
Look for smooth connections that bend, especially in interpolated instances.

A kink can look fine in both masters and appear halfway between them. Kink Finder reports them across the designspace.

checks.title: Place points at the extremes
checks.info:
Check that every curve has nodes at its topmost, bottommost, leftmost and rightmost points.

Missing extremes affect rendering at small sizes, break hinting, and make interpolation less predictable. Red Arrow marks them in the edit view.

checks.title: Check for zero handles
checks.info:
Look for offcurve points sitting on their oncurve point, with the handle pulled in to zero length.

Some rendering engines mishandle them, and interpolation gives odd results. Red Arrow marks them in the edit view.

checks.title: Check that terminals are consistent
checks.info:
Compare stroke endings across the font for angle, weight and shape.

Terminals carry much of the family's character, so an odd one looks like a mistake rather than a variation.

checks.title: Check that diagonals are consistent
checks.info:
Compare the diagonal strokes of v, w, x, y, k and their relatives for weight and angle.

Diagonals need optical correction to look as heavy as vertical stems, and the correction has to be applied the same way throughout.

checks.title: Check that path directions are correct
checks.info:
Check that outer contours and counters run in the right directions.

Wrong directions fill in the counters. Static exports fix this when overlaps are removed, so it mainly matters for variable fonts, where nothing corrects it.

checks.title: Draw a custom .notdef
checks.info:
Draw a .notdef glyph in every master instead of leaving it to the automatic fallback.

.notdef is what readers see when a character is missing from the font. Glyphs makes a plain box at export; a drawn one matches the design.

checks.title: Check that the space has an appropriate width
checks.info:
Test the space in running text at several weights, and check that the no-break space has the same width.

The space sets the rhythm of the line. Too narrow and words run together, too wide and the text opens up. Only reading it settles the value.

checks.title: Add the space characters the font needs
checks.info:
Check for the usual set: no-break space, figure space, thin space, hair space, em and en space, punctuation space, zero-width space.

Layout applications and web text use these for fixed spacing. Build Space Glyphs adds them with metrics keys already set.

checks.title: Remove empty exporting glyphs
checks.info:
Look for glyphs set to export that have no paths, no components and no width.

These are usually glyphs that were added and never drawn. In the exported font they become zero-width characters.

checks.title: Keep brace layers inside the designspace
checks.info:
Check that each brace layer's coordinates fall inside the range the masters cover.

A brace layer outside that range never activates, so the substitution it was drawn for does not happen.

checks.title: Check for nested and flipped components
checks.info:
Look for components built from other composites, and for components mirrored with a negative scale.

Both can behave badly at export and in interpolation. Component Problem Finder reports them along with other component issues.

checks.title: Check that diacritics align on their base shapes
checks.info:
Read accented letters in a text tab across all masters and watch how the marks sit over the bases.

Anchors place marks by coordinate. Optical centring is a separate judgement, and a mark centred on the bounding box often looks off on a diagonal or asymmetric letter.

checks.title: Check that anchors are consistent
checks.info:
Check that base letters have the anchors their marks attach to, and that marks have the matching underscore anchors.

Anchors drive automatic composite alignment and the mark features. A missing one puts a diacritic in the wrong place, or leaves that letter out of the feature.

checks.title: Set up the ligature carets
checks.info:
Add caret anchors to every ligature made by liga, dlig, rlig, clig or hlig. A ligature of two parts needs one caret.

Carets tell text editors where the cursor can sit inside a ligature. Without them the cursor jumps over the whole ligature.

checks.title: Bring the metrics keys back in sync
checks.info:
Look for layers whose sidebearings no longer match their metrics keys. Glyphs shows these in red.

An out-of-sync key means the sidebearing was changed by hand after the key was set, so the key no longer describes the spacing and later changes will not carry over.

checks.title: Check that no characters are touching
checks.info:
Look for glyph pairs whose outlines touch or overlap once kerning is applied.

Touché scans the font for collisions and lists the pairs it finds.

checks.title: Check kerning against the brace and bracket layers
checks.info:
Check the glyphs with alternate layers at the points where those layers take over.

Kerning is set on the default outlines, but a bracket layer can change the shape, so a pair that fits in the Regular may collide once the alternate appears.

checks.title: Remove tiny kerning pairs
checks.info:
Look through the kerning for pairs below about 5 units and consider removing them.

A correction that small is not visible at text sizes, and it adds file size and noise when the kerning is reviewed later.

checks.title: Check for overkerns
checks.info:
Look for pairs kerned by more than a reasonable share of the glyph widths.

Extreme values are usually typos or leftover experiments. New Tab with Overkerned Pairs collects them in one tab.

checks.title: Consider whether extension kerning is needed
checks.info:
Decide how far the kerning should go beyond the core alphabet: punctuation, figures, brackets, quotes and their classes.

Many of the spacing problems readers notice sit at these boundaries rather than between two letters. How far to take it depends on what the family is for.

checks.title: Name the stylistic sets
checks.info:
Give every ssXX feature a name in Font Info > Features.

Applications show that name in their stylistic set menu. Without one the menu shows 'ss03'.

checks.title: Extend the stylistic sets to related glyphs
checks.info:
Check that composites and diacritics built from a glyph with a stylistic variant have their own variant.

If a.ss01 exists but aacute.ss01 does not, switching the feature on changes some letters and leaves the accented ones as they were.

checks.title: Cover all uppercase with small caps
checks.info:
Check that every uppercase letter has a small cap counterpart.

A missing one falls back to the full capital, which is taller than everything around it in small cap text.

checks.title: Give all tabular glyphs the same width
checks.info:
Check that every glyph with a tabular suffix has the same width as the others in its group, in every master.

Figures that do not line up in columns are not tabular. Groups are compared separately, so .tf and .tf.sc each keep their own width.

checks.title: Make the math symbols tabular
checks.info:
Check that plus, minus, equals, multiply, divide and the rest share the tabular width.

Math symbols sit in columns of figures, so a symbol of a different width breaks the alignment. Tabular Checker reports the ones that differ.

checks.title: Check the fraction numerators, denominators and slash
checks.info:
Read the precomposed fractions and the frac feature: how numerator and denominator align, and how the fraction slash spaces against them.

Fractions are assembled from parts that were drawn separately, so they need looking at as a whole.

checks.title: Compile the feature code without errors
checks.info:
Compile the OpenType features and read the errors reported for features, prefixes and classes.

Hand-written code can break without any obvious sign, and a broken feature usually just does not apply.

checks.title: Confirm the intended language coverage
checks.info:
Check which languages the character set supports against the list the project promised.

One missing accented letter drops a language. Hyperglot compares a character set against its language database.

checks.title: Test style linking in real applications
checks.info:
Install a test export and try the Bold and Italic buttons in Word, the style menus in Adobe apps, and the macOS font pickers.

Style linking is defined in the file but each application interprets it, so it has to be tried.

checks.title: Test real exports in InDesign and a browser
checks.info:
Export the OTF, TTF and variable versions and open them in InDesign and a browser before release.

This catches problems no source-level check can see: compilation faults, features that do not apply, rendering surprises.

checks.title: Test the WOFF files in the relevant browsers
checks.info:
Load the webfont exports in the browsers the project cares about and read real text.

Browsers differ in rendering, spacing and feature support, and some problems appear only once the file is served as a webfont.

checks.title: Run the files through Fontspector
checks.info:
Run the compiled binaries through Fontspector before release.

It inspects the exported tables, which is the layer this checklist does not reach. Source files can be fine while the binary still fails a check.
